objects.description: One line of the chart of accounts. Category and holder_id together are its identity, and it is opened lazily by its first posting rather than because its holder registered.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: code
fields.description: The account number a chart of accounts is laid out by, such as 1000 for cash. Supplied by the caller and never minted here; optional, and unique across the ledger when it is given.

fields.name: name
fields.description: The account's title as a ledger prints it, such as 'Cash at bank'. Free text the caller chooses.

fields.name: category
fields.description: What sort of account this is, in the calling domain's own words — a member's account, a paybill's basket, a school's fee account. Deliberately open: which categories exist is the part that differs between a membership organisation, a school and a token ledger, so this module never validates it against a fixed list.

fields.name: type
fields.description: The account's place in the accounting equation, and so its normal balance. The one closed vocabulary here, because it is double-entry theory itself rather than a decision any one domain gets to make differently.

fields.name: holder_id
fields.description: The subject this subsidiary account is kept for — a member, a paybill, a student, a wallet address. An opaque id the caller supplies and interprets; this module never reads it for meaning, only for identity.

fields.name: opened_at
fields.description: When the first posting opened the account. Written by the store, never by a caller.

fields.name: closed_at
fields.description: When the account was closed. The only value on an account that ever changes, and it is refused while a balance remains.

indexes.name: identity
indexes.description: Enforces one account per (category, holder_id), which is what makes opening idempotent rather than a pre-check-then-insert race.

indexes.name: code
indexes.description: Backs the refusal of a code some other account already carries. Not declared unique, because every account without a code stores the empty string rather than null and they would all collide on one constraint.

indexes.name: opened
indexes.description: Orders the account listing oldest-opened first.

objects.description: One journal entry: an amount debited to exactly one account and credited to exactly one other. Append-only — there is no update and no delete, and a mistake is corrected by a new entry naming the original in reverses_entry_id.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: posted_at
fields.description: When it hit the books. Written by the store, never by a caller.

fields.name: occurred_at
fields.description: When the underlying event happened. A read that orders a ledger orders on this, falling back to posted_at where it is absent.

fields.name: due_at
fields.description: When what the entry records falls due, as an RFC 3339 instant. Absent means the entry has no due date and is never overdue. The overdue read ages from this rather than from when the entry was posted.

fields.name: debit_account_id
fields.description: The account debited. Every entry names both sides; there is no one-sided posting in this ledger.

fields.name: credit_account_id
fields.description: The account credited, for the same amount, which is what makes the entry balance.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The amount posted to both sides, in the deployment's smallest denominated unit, always positive. Which side is which is the two accounts, never a sign, so no posting can change the sum of every balance in the ledger.

fields.name: document_kind
fields.description: What sort of source document caused the posting — an invoice, a receipt, a statement import — in the calling domain's own words. Open for the same reason category is: this module enforces that every entry names one, never which ones exist.

fields.name: document_id
fields.description: The source document that caused the posting.

fields.name: actor_id
fields.description: Who or what caused the posting, never only a role. The ledger is an accountability surface, so this is required.

fields.name: narration
fields.description: The sentence the ledger reads back against this entry; on a correction, the reason for the reversal.

fields.name: dimensions
fields.description: Further facts the posting is analysed by, as a flat object of named keys to text values — a department, a cost centre, a project, a fiscal year. The caller chooses both the keys and the values; this module never learns what any of them mean. Each key is lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters; each value is non-empty text of at most 200 characters with no control characters; at most 16 keys. An entry's dimensions narrow a listing and a balance without a separate account per combination. Absent means the entry carries none.

fields.name: reverses_entry_id
fields.description: The entry this one corrects, or empty. The original is never touched, and an entry may be reversed at most once — a second reversal would drift the ledger off zero-sum.

fields.name: settles_entry_id
fields.description: The charge entry this one pays, or empty. It must name an entry already in the ledger. The overdue read nets every unreversed entry settling a charge against that charge's amount, so a paid charge stops reading as overdue and a part-paid one reads with what is still outstanding.

indexes.name: debit_account
indexes.description: Reads the debit side of one account's ledger, which every balance and listing folds.

indexes.name: credit_account
indexes.description: Reads the credit side of the same.

indexes.name: reverses
indexes.description: Answers 'has this entry already been reversed' without scanning the ledger, which is the check that keeps a correction from being applied twice.

indexes.name: settles
indexes.description: Finds the entries paying a charge without scanning the ledger, which is what the overdue read nets against.

objects.description: What one account is expected to hold over one period. Kept beside the ledger rather than as a second account, so a variance is one read rather than two balances. Setting a budget again for the same account and period replaces its amount.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: account_id
fields.description: The account the budget is set against.

fields.name: period_start
fields.description: The first instant of the period, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 instant.

fields.name: period_end
fields.description: The instant the period ends, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 instant after period_start.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the budget line is called, such as Road repair.

fields.name: department
fields.description: The department the budget line belongs to, such as Public works.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The budgeted balance for the period, in the same smallest unit and the same debit-minus-credit sense as the account's balance.

fields.name: follow_milestones
fields.description: Whether the line is followed milestone by milestone. Off by default; a reader shows the line's milestones and payment certificates only when it is on.

fields.name: cost_shares
fields.description: How the line's spending falls on neighbourhoods, as a flat object of neighbourhood name to whole percent. The percents are positive and sum to 100. Absent means the cost is counted in one: each spending entry stays with the neighbourhood it names.

fields.name: set_at
fields.description: When the amount was last set. Written by the store, never by a caller.

indexes.name: period
indexes.description: Enforces one budget per account and period, which is what makes setting a budget a replace rather than a second row.

objects.description: One stage of a contract that a budget line pays for, such as the foundations of a school extension. Planned against the account that carries the spending, it is paid only through certificates, and it reads as certified once its certificates add up to its amount.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: account_id
fields.description: The account the spending is booked to when a certificate is issued.

fields.name: contract_id
fields.description: The contract the milestone belongs to. An opaque id the caller supplies and interprets; this module only groups milestones by it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the milestone delivers, in the caller's words.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: What the milestone is worth in total, in the smallest unit, always positive.

fields.name: due_at
fields.description: When the milestone is planned to be reached, as an RFC 3339 instant.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Where the milestone stands. Written by the store: planned until the first certificate, part_certified while certificates cover less than the amount, certified once they cover all of it.

fields.name: certified_amount
fields.description: The sum of the certificates issued against the milestone. Written by the store, never by a caller.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the milestone was recorded. Written by the store, never by a caller.

objects.description: A payment certificate: a named person confirming that a milestone's work, or part of it, is done and payable. Issuing one posts the net payment and the retention to the ledger. Append-only apart from the release of its retention.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: milestone_id
fields.description: The milestone being certified.

fields.name: payee_account_id
fields.description: The account credited with the net payment, and later with the released retention.

fields.name: retention_account_id
fields.description: The account that holds the retention until it is released.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The gross amount certified, before retention, always positive.

fields.name: retention_bps
fields.description: The share of the gross amount withheld, in hundredths of a percent, from 0 to 5000.

fields.name: retention_amount
fields.description: What was withheld, rounded down. Written by the store.

fields.name: payment_entry_id
fields.description: The ledger entry paying the amount less the retention. Written by the store.

fields.name: retention_entry_id
fields.description: The ledger entry setting the retention aside, empty when nothing was withheld. Written by the store.

fields.name: certified_by
fields.description: Who certified the work, never only a role.

fields.name: certified_at
fields.description: When the certificate was issued. Written by the store.

fields.name: release_due_at
fields.description: The earliest instant the retention may be released, as an RFC 3339 instant. Absent when nothing was withheld.

fields.name: released_at
fields.description: When the retention was paid out. Empty while it is still held.

fields.name: release_entry_id
fields.description: The ledger entry paying the retention out. Empty while it is still held.

indexes.name: milestone
indexes.description: Lists the certificates of one milestone.

objects.description: A request to buy something, drawn against one budget line, that suppliers answer with quotes. Append-only: it is recorded once and read back with the quotes offered for it.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: budget_id
fields.description: The budget line the purchase draws on.

fields.name: title
fields.description: What is bought, in the caller's words, such as Resurfacing of Mill Street.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The specification suppliers quote against.

fields.name: closes_at
fields.description: When quotes stop being invited, as an RFC 3339 instant. Absent when no date is set.

fields.name: created_by
fields.description: Who opened the tender, supplied by the mount.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the tender was recorded. Written by the store.

indexes.name: budget
indexes.description: Lists the tenders drawing on one budget line.

objects.description: One supplier's offer for a tender. Append-only: a supplier that changes its offer sends another quote.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: tender_id
fields.description: The tender the offer answers.

fields.name: supplier
fields.description: Who makes the offer, as the supplier is named.

fields.name: amount
fields.description: The price offered in the smallest unit, always positive.

fields.name: note
fields.description: What the offer includes or assumes.

fields.name: valid_until
fields.description: The last instant the price holds, as an RFC 3339 instant. Absent when it has no end.

fields.name: quoted_by
fields.description: Who recorded the quote, supplied by the mount.

fields.name: quoted_at
fields.description: When the quote was recorded. Written by the store.

indexes.name: tender
indexes.description: Lists the quotes offered for one tender.

objects.description: A financial report as it stood when it was sent upward: the totals and department figures folded at that moment, and the budget lines when the kind keeps them. Append-only: a second send of the same period and kind is another record.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Storage key, opaque to callers.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: Which report was sent. budget_and_actuals keeps every budget line beside the figures; spending_by_department keeps the department figures only.

fields.name: period_start
fields.description: The first instant of the period reported, inclusive, as an RFC 3339 instant, exactly as the budget lines were set.

fields.name: period_end
fields.description: The instant the period reported ends, exclusive, as an RFC 3339 instant, exactly as the budget lines were set.

fields.name: planned
fields.description: The planned total of the period as sent.

fields.name: spent
fields.description: The spent total of the period as sent.

fields.name: difference
fields.description: Planned minus spent as sent.

fields.name: departments
fields.description: The planned, spent and difference figures of each department as sent, the difference being planned minus spent.

fields.name: lines
fields.description: Every budget line of the period as sent. Absent for the kinds that do not keep them.

fields.name: sent_by
fields.description: Who sent the report, supplied by the mount.

fields.name: sent_at
fields.description: When the report was sent. Written by the store.

indexes.name: sent
indexes.description: Lists the sent reports newest first.
